title: The Word 'Algorithm' Comes From a Person's Name (9th century)
explainer: 'Algorithm' is not an abstract coinage — it is a distorted Latin rendering of the name of al-Khwarizmi, the 9th-century Baghdad mathematician whose book on Hindu-Arabic arithmetic taught step-by-step calculation procedures. For centuries the related word 'algorism' specifically meant the written procedure for doing arithmetic with that number system, and it only broadened to today's general sense of 'any step-by-step procedure' as computing developed in the 20th century.

title: Euclid's Algorithm: a Procedure Older Than Writing Paper (c. 300 BCE)
explainer: Long before the word 'algorithm' existed, Euclid's Elements (Book VII) described a precise, finite procedure for finding the greatest common divisor of two numbers by repeated subtraction — a method some historians believe may predate Euclid himself by a century or two. It is often cited as the oldest nontrivial algorithm still in common use, and it is a clean illustration that algorithmic thinking, breaking a problem into exact, repeatable steps, existed millennia before computers did.
